tool_args.rationale: The open-branch observations show a strong gradient-dependent change, confirming the bridge/flux ambiguity, while the remaining trajectory conditions are fixed. A fine trajectory batch is the most relevant available measurement to separate a static saturation law from coupled transfer dynamics before fitting.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a saturating response with a linear sink-gradient correction
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Seven rows constrain the u_now response, but only two open-branch points vary s_grad; this flexible fit would not identify the bridge coupling reliably.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a two-layer coupled ODE immediately
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All rows share H, u_past, x_now, and mem_conv, so the trajectory data do not yet distinguish transfer dynamics from a static response.
It is explicitly irrelevant to identifying the predictive law and has higher cost.
